instructions: Peel the 1 1/2 lbs potatoes and cut them into 1 1/2 inch chunks. Add them to a large pot with 8 cups cold water and 1 tsp of the salt.
Bring the potatoes to a boil over high heat, then turn the heat down to a steady simmer. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until a fork slides into a chunk with no resistance.
Meanwhile, turn the oven to 200°F and set a wire rack on a baking sheet. Finely chop the onion and mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Shred half the lettuce thinly and crumble the 4 oz cotija.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, for 5 to 6 minutes, until it's soft and golden at the edges. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant. Take the pan off the heat.
Drain the potatoes well and add them to the skillet. Add the last 3/4 tsp salt and mash everything together until smooth.
Taste the filling. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spread the filling out on a plate and leave it for about 10 minutes, until it's barely warm. Hot filling makes the tortillas soggy. Wipe out the skillet.
Wrap the 16 tortillas in a damp kitchen towel and microwave them for 45 to 60 seconds, until they're soft and bend without cracking.
Spread about 3 tbsp of the filling over one half of each tortilla. Fold it over into a half moon and pin the open edge with a toothpick.

Pour the remaining 1 cup oil into the skillet and heat it over medium high. You're aiming for 350°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it. No thermometer? Dip the edge of a taco in. It's ready when it sizzles straight away.
Fry the tacos 4 at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp. Flip them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes. Stand back a little. They can spatter.
Lift them onto the rack and keep them warm in the oven while you fry the rest.
Pull out the toothpicks and top each taco with the lettuce and the cotija.
Serve with the sour cream and the salsa.
method_notes: Every version boils peeled potatoes, mashes them, folds the mash into warmed corn tortillas pinned with a toothpick and shallow fries them until crisp. Mexican Made Meatless softens onion and garlic in oil and mashes the potatoes into them, and tops the tacos with lettuce, cotija, salsa and sour cream; Kitchen Gidget and Mama Maggie's Kitchen keep the filling to potato, salt and pepper. This follows the lead, scaled from 1 lb to 1 1/2 lbs potatoes for 16 tacos so four tacos make a dinner, with a jar of tomato salsa standing in for the lead's homemade one.
